facts.heading: Long working day routine
facts.content: Daniel works as a project manager at a logistics company. He stays at his desk until ten at night answering messages. He thinks about work even when not working.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night. Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Terrible sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible. He sleeps about four hours most nights. He wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours. I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Waking up at three AM
facts.content: When Daniel wakes up at three, he has to start work tasks. He checks shipping schedules and client details. He looks at the clock and plans for minimal sleep.
facts.evidence: We have to start. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something. And I look at the clock and I do the mountain how little sleep I'm gonna get which makes it worse.

facts.heading: Dreading the nights
facts.content: Daniel started dreading the nights. He lies until about five and then gets up to make tea.
facts.evidence: Then I lie until about five and get up and make tea. I started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn. This is a significant event alongside his work stress.
facts.evidence: my father. His diagnosis, Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Involved in father's care
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments occur every few weeks, requiring an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds, neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Guilt about caregiving
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty about his involvement in his father's care. He feels selfish for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it. He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Sister provides support
facts.content: Daniel's younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto. She calls their father every Sunday. Hannah is not the one neglecting him but is hearing about it.
facts.evidence: My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father Who falls on me? She calls him every Sunday. She's not the one who's neglecting him. Just the one who's hearing.

facts.heading: Avoiding sharing feelings

facts.heading: Desire to communicate truth

facts.evidence: What would she want her to know if you said it? That I'm not fine. That someday I sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before I go in because I can't
